KEY MESSAGE 1...A powerful coastal storm will continue to bring 
severe impacts to the region through today into this evening due to 
damaging high winds accompanied by heavy rainfall. The storm departs 
overnight into Friday. 

Synoptics:

As of 130 PM, low pressure was located near the border of North 
Carolina and Virginia while continuing to deepen and move northward. 
Meanwhile a strong and expansive high to our north continues to 
depart into the Canadian Maritimes. It is the pressure gradient 
between these two features that's causing the winds to be so strong 
and so far, things are panning out as forecast. There has been tidal 
flooding (see coastal flooding section below) and we are just 
starting to get into the strongest winds as a powerful LLJ is moving 
in from the south. Generally speaking, still expecting widespread 
northeast to east winds of 25 to 45 mph this afternoon (strongest 
near the coast and Delmarva ) with gusts of 50 to 70 mph (again, 
strongest near the coast and Delmarva). Storm impacts are discussed 
in further detail below:

Impacts:

Winds: The most severe impact from this storm aside from coastal 
flooding (see separate coastal flooding key message below) will be 
from damaging high winds. Winds have been ramping up steadily going 
into this afternoon and expect the strongest winds to be through 
this afternoon into early this evening. While things are largely 
panning out as forecast, winds/gusts have been slower to ramp up 
over our northern zones from Berks County northeast through the 
Lehigh Vally into northwest New Jersey. While it's possible some of 
these areas may not get quite to High Wind Warning criteria it 
should still be be close and impacts are still likely especially 
when combined with the heavy rainfall. Farther south, we've already 
seen peak wind gusts of 60-70+ mph over Delmarva into coastal NJ. So 
the expectation is that widespread wind gusts of 50-70 mph will
continue through the afternoon for most of the area before the 
winds diminish south to north through the evening period into 
the early overnight. As mentioned, winds in our northern zones 
will be in the lower end of this range and for Sussex County NJ 
(where there's a Wind Advisory) gusts will generally max out 
around 45-55 mph. Elsewhere, the High Wind Warning remains in 
effect through the evening. We've already been getting damage 
reports and expect widespread tree damage and power outages 
will continue to be an issue, especially near the coast and over
Delmarva where peak gusts may continue to exceed 70 mph.

While the winds will subside for a time tonight, they will pick back 
up again for Friday with southwest winds potentially gusting 30 to 
40 mph. This may hamper clean up efforts. 

Rainfall/flooding threat: Given recent dryness and the progressive 
nature of this system, freshwater flooding does not appear to be as 
significant of a concern (compared to the high winds and tidal 
flooding). However we do expect near and S/E of the urban corridor a 
widespread 2 to 4 inches is likely with locally over 4 inches 
possible, especially over Delmarva and coastal NJ. The Weather 
Prediction Center has all of the area in at least a MARGINAL risk 
for excessive rainfall with a SLIGHT risk along the coast north and 
west through the I-95 corridor. The biggest threat will be urban 
flooding as well as flooding of low lying and poor drainage areas. 
Some of the more sensitive creeks and streams could also exceed 
flood stage. Finally, the heavy rain will exacerbate the coastal 
flooding issues. The heaviest rain will fall this afternoon into the 
first part of the evening before it starts to taper off. Some 
showers are likely to linger on Friday, especially northwest of I-
95, but any rainfall on Friday will be inconsequential.

Severe Weather: Areas across southern Delmarva just south of our 
county warning area are in a Marginal threat for severe 
thunderstorms per SPC. The period of concern will be late this 
afternoon into the early evening as Delmarva gets into the system's 
warm sector for several hours. So while we currently don't expect 
any severe storms to be in our area this potential will have to be 
watched closely in case there's a shift farther north. This marginal 
severe threat area (again, currently south of our forecast area) 
does include a 2% tornado threat. 

Precip type: There's been some wintry precipitation at the onset at 
Mount Pocono but temperatures there are 33 degrees at this time and 
expect them to continue rising this afternoon changing things to 
rain. Otherwise, all rain elsewhere. 

Timing: Heaviest rain and strongest winds through early this 
evening before the low starts pulling away. 

Friday will be windy (winds not nearly as strong as today) with some 
showers around. Even Saturday will be breezy (but less so than 
Friday) but otherwise the weather over the weekend will be more 
tranquil. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Significant tidal flooding is expected
